evidence: src/application/dtos.ts declares CreateProductInput/ProductDto, used only by InventoryService, and CreateOrderInput/OrderDto, used only by OrderService.
src/application/inventory-service.ts: InventoryService takes a ProductRepository in its constructor and maps to ProductDto via private toDto.

src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService.placeOrder checks and reserves stock through product.canReserve and product.reserve; cancelOrder uses order.cancel and product.release, so the stock rules stay in the domain.
src/application/order-service.ts: normaliseLines is the single place where order items are validated and merged; requireOrder and requireProduct are the single places for not-found handling.
Both services follow the same pattern: repository access, a domain operation, then a private toDto mapping; neither reaches into infrastructure.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module is one cohesive application-service layer. dtos.ts defines the inputs and outputs for the use cases. InventoryService (addProduct, listProducts) and OrderService (placeOrder, advanceOrder, cancelOrder, listOrders) coordinate domain objects through the ProductRepository and OrderRepository interfaces they receive in their constructors. Both services use the same pattern: repository access, then a domain operation, then a private toDto mapping. Stock rules are handled by domain methods (canReserve, reserve, release), and order state changes by Order methods (advanceTo, cancel); the services do not reimplement them. Rules that live in the services appear only once within the unit: item validation and merging in normaliseLines, not-found handling in requireOrder and requireProduct, and the duplicate-product check in addProduct. The one repetition is the inline item type { productId, quantity } in CreateOrderInput and OrderDto. That is repeated type structure, not a duplicated rule. Whether the customer and quantity checks are repeated in the domain can't be confirmed from the material given.
